Kaipo Olsen-Baker Named World Rugby Women's Player of the Year

01 Nov 2026, 10:48 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Recognition for the Black Ferns

New Zealand's Kaipo Olsen-Baker has been awarded the World Rugby Women's Player of the Year title. The 24-year-old number eight, noted for her impact as a ball carrier, secured the honor after a competitive season representing the Black Ferns.

Olsen-Baker was selected for the award ahead of three other finalists:

  • DaLeaka Menin (Canada)
  • Megan Jones (England)
  • Zoe Harrison (England)

Performance Context

Under the leadership of new head coach Whitney Hansen, the Black Ferns experienced a strong run in 2026. The team’s only defeat during the calendar year was a 26-19 loss to England in September. Olsen-Baker played a central role in the squad's successful campaign, which notably included a victory in the Pacific Four Series, a competition featuring Canada, Australia, and the United States.

Additional Accolades

Beyond the top player award, World Rugby recognized emerging talent within the New Zealand squad. Flanker Elinor-Plum King was named Breakthrough Player of the Year. The 22-year-old recorded three Test tries during her inaugural season at the international level.

Official Statements

World Rugby chair Brett Robinson praised the impact of both athletes during the awards ceremony held in Christchurch. Robinson noted the consistency displayed by Olsen-Baker and the rapid progression of King as key factors in their respective honors.

Verification

The details of these awards, including the winners and the criteria mentioned, can be verified through the official World Rugby website or their verified social media channels. The original announcement was conducted in Christchurch to commemorate the conclusion of the international season.
